Funding Proposal for Operations: July 2024
metadata.description:
# Funding Proposal for Operations: July 2024
As per the discussions we had in the below governance forum we are putting a formal Tally proposal in front of INT DAO to fund the Operations Multisig which can be used to run day to day operations and also used to complete the 24 week IFT airdrop effort. 

<https://gov.theinternettoken.com/t/operations-multisig-summary-and-top-up-till-august/60>

Details about the ask, justification and reporting can be found in the above proposal.

**Overall Budget:** 11m INT and 3 ETH

* Airdrops for Weeks 6-24: 9m INT
* Contributor backpay and reimbursements: 0.5 ETH and 680k INT
* Support Contributor payments for June and July and buffer for any other small marketing needs: 2.5 ETH and 1,320,000 INT
* Support Protocol Farming: As needed

This request covers past obligations for May, June and July. Any funds remaining will rollover to the next period. A review and a new budget proposal will be initiated in early September. DAO can decide whether they would like to continue this model or suggest alternative proposals.

The multisig address is base:0x0C02d2D320C62d4088840a459fE8862C802fbA78

It is a 4/7 multisig. You can view the multisig holdings and transactions on basescan.org or via the Safe website.

<https://app.safe.global/home?safe=base:0x0C02d2D320C62d4088840a459fE8862C802fbA78>

metadata.description:
# Award Bounty for exclusion: 0x5d64d14d2cf4fe5fe4e65b1c7e3d11e18d493091
Vote For, to award a bounty, if the account 0x5d64d14d2cf4fe5fe4e65b1c7e3d11e18d493091 was usefully excluded.

Usefully excluded refers to: The excluded account must be related to a frequently used DEX or aggregator,
AND exclusion of the account is necessary to avoid loss of tickets from regular user action,
AND the example transaction clearly demonstrates a user losing a ticket through regular DEX or aggregator usage.

Regular DEX or aggregator usage refers to: Usage of the DEX or aggregator in a way that matches the official interface.

metadata.title: Exclude New Uniswap FeeCollector
metadata.description:
# Exclude New Uniswap FeeCollector
With the Uniswap fee switch turned on, INT tokens are transferred from the INT/WETH pool to the Uniswap Router then to the Uniswap FeeCollector. Uniswap has deployed a new FeeCollector contract, so this contract should be marked as excluded to avoid tickets being sent to it.

metadata.title: # Deploy API3 Quintessence VRF Provider
metadata.description:
# Deploy API3 Quintessence VRF Provider
Currently, the random value generated is provided by Quantum Blockchains: <https://docs.api3.org/reference/qrng/providers.html#quantum-blockchains-random-numbers>



There were two occurrences so far where there were delays for results from this provider.



API3 has recommended to try using the Quintessence provider instead: <https://docs.api3.org/reference/qrng/providers.html#quintessence-quantum-random-numbers>



This proposal uses the INT VRF Factory to deploy an INT Quintessence VRF provider.



Note that this only deploys the provider, a separate proposal would need to be created to configure the RewardDistributor (https://basescan.org/address/0x76BfDDf9D9aD158cc47d4abba5af7f16A922f865) to use the new provider after it has been deployed.



Parameters in this proposal used for deployment:



* salt: 0x0c5fa5513e87c393092aabcfb02bee4f499a38e1f5807436b901af19e85302ee

This is the hash of "API3-Quintessence" on <https://emn178.github.io/online-tools/keccak_256.html>



* vrfConsumer: 0x76BfDDf9D9aD158cc47d4abba5af7f16A922f865

This is the RewardDistributor, the current INT Api3VrfProvider (https://basescan.org/address/0x2e2e91b4dE929ef1D32425ad6A2b0c620eAb591E#readContract) has the same value for vrfConsumer



* airnodeRrp: 0xa0AD79D995DdeeB18a14eAef56A549A04e3Aa1Bd

This is the API3 airnodeRrp contract address on Base, <https://docs.api3.org/reference/airnode/latest/#airnoderrpv0>, the current INT Api3VrfProvider has the same value for airnodeRrp



* airnode: 0x224e030f03Cd3440D88BD78C9BF5Ed36458A1A25

This is the airnode for Quintessence <https://docs.api3.org/reference/qrng/providers.html#quintessence-quantum-random-numbers>



* endpointIdUint256: 0xffd1bbe880e7b2c662f6c8511b15ff22d12a4a35d5c8c17202893a5f10e25284

This is the endpointIdUint256 for Quintessence <https://docs.api3.org/reference/qrng/providers.html#quintessence-quantum-random-numbers>

metadata.title: # Set BaseURI for IFT Contract
metadata.description:
# Set BaseURI for IFT Contract
In order for Infinity Collection NFTs to display an image when shown in NFT marketplaces or wallets, we need to set a baseURI for the IFT contract. This will ensure that third-parties can call the tokenURI function on the contract and retrieve a standard ERC-721 JSON metadata file. Within that file is a path to the IFT image. For the time being, all IFTs will display the same image, but in the near future, artwork will likely be commissioned for certain segments/collections. At that time we can update the pointers for the individual IFTs to the unique artwork.

metadata.title: # Set BaseURI for Ticket Contract
metadata.description:
# Set BaseURI for Ticket Contract
In order for Ticket NFTs to display an image when shown in NFT marketplaces or wallets, we need to set a baseURI for the Ticket NFT contract. This will ensure that third-parties can call the tokenURI function on the contract and retrieve a standard ERC-721 JSON metadata file. Within that file is a path to the TKT image. Ticket NFTs are somewhat ephemeral, but this will hopefully help with getting the NFT image visible to third-party sites like Debank etc.

metadata.title: # Reduce quorum percentage
metadata.description:
# Reduce quorum percentage
A proposal passes only if majority of the votes are "For" the proposal, and if the quorum is reached.



Quorum is determined as (quorum percentage) \* (INT total supply)



The current quorum percentage is 4%, the INT total supply is 894m, so current quorum is 35.7m.



Since majority of INT is in the treasury and the Uniswap pool, the circulating supply of INT is 157m.



Which means that the effective quorum percentage is 35.7 / 157 = 22%.



This is a relatively high number and there is a risk that if tokens are undelegated, the total delegated tokens may be less than required for quorum leading to the DAO being bricked.



This proposal proposes to reduce the quorum percentage to 3%, which would reduce the required quorum to 26.8m



Even with the reduced quorum percentage, proposals will still require a majority "For" vote to pass

metadata.title: # Add an automatic exclusion process
metadata.description:
# Add an automatic exclusion process
Currently, it takes 8 days for a contract to be excluded from receiving tickets, this can cause issues if the addresses of DEXes or aggregators change.



Uniswap updates their router somewhat frequently, and with the latest change it took 8 days to exclude the relevant contracts. This led to tickets being sent to the Uniswap router during that time.



There is a new ExclusionAutomator contract at: <https://basescan.org/address/0xD8dDe734E22b9B2785a47BFd9A45fF4c3C6087d1#code>



From the contract:



`// allows anyone to put up a bond to exclude an exchange / aggregator contract`

`// from receiving tickets`

`//`

`// process:`

`//`

`// 1. call addExcludedFeeAccount(account, exampleTransactionHash)`

`//     - account: the contract account to exclude`

`//     - exampleTransactionHash: an example transaction hash to show that the`

`//     specified contract receives ticket under regular user usage`

`//     - value: a msg value that is more than or equal to the getBondAmount()`

`//     value needs to be paid to call this function`

`//     - the specified account will be immediately excluded from receiving`

`//     tickets`

`//`

`// 2. a governance proposal will automatically be created to refund the caller`

`//    of the addExcludedFeeAccount function as well as award a bounty`

`//`

`// the bondValue should be configured to be large enough such that it would be`

`// costly for any user to call addExcludedFeeAccount on smart contract accounts`

`//`

`// addExcludedFeeAccount validates that the specified account is a contract`

`// so it is not possible to use the contract to exclude regular accounts from`

`// receiving tickets`



The bond value of the contract is currently 5000 USD worth of ETH and the reward amount per valid exclusion is the lower of 100 USD / 0.1 ETH



The ExclusionAutomator contract requires 1,000,000 INT to have sufficient voting power to create the bounty proposal, it also requires the CONFIG\_ADMIN role



This proposal if passed, transfers 1,000,000 INT to the ExclusionAutomator contract and grants it the CONFIG\_ADMIN role

# Add support for Aggregators

# Overview

Aggregators were previously blacklisted because tickets were being minted to the aggregator contracts.

There is a newly deployed TradeFeeCallback contract that allows aggregators to be supported:

<https://basescan.org/address/0x159884b1Af3Bd6C3e4993E15490E55C0F3a10117#code>

// support aggregators by storing fee paid as pendingFeePaid
// supported aggregators would need to be added to _excludedFeeAccounts
// the contract will skip recording fee paid to these excluded addresses
// and store the fee paid in pendingFeePaid
// the pending fee paid will be credited to the receiver on the next token

metadata.title: # Update Timelock Delay to 1 Day
metadata.description:
# Update Timelock Delay to 1 Day
The current timelock delay is set to 3 days: <https://basescan.org/address/0xE05dD5B785f578337B2B8F695Fbc521669c69403#readContract>



minDelay: 259200 (259200 / 60 / 60 / 24 = 3)



Since governance voting duration is 7 days in total, this leads to 10 days required for changes to be in effect



Reduce the timelock delay to 24 hours (24 \* 60 \* 60 = 86400) to allow changes to be made in 8 days instead

Users are informed not to use a DEX aggregator to purchase INT

Help prevent user error by blacklisting the DEX aggregator addresses on Base
